metadata.name: box
metadata.description: (w, h, d) - a box geometry SPEC node ({spec:'box', w,h,d}). Pure - the Three geometry is built by the replayer, never here. =scene(..., mesh(box(1,1,1), material('#4a90d9'))).

metadata.name: sphere
metadata.description: (r) - a sphere geometry SPEC node ({spec:'sphere', r}).

metadata.name: material
metadata.description: (color) - a material SPEC node ({spec:'material', color}). Lambert-shaded by the replayer.

metadata.name: mesh
metadata.description: (geometry, material) - a single-object mesh SPEC node. For N copies use instances().

metadata.name: light
metadata.description: (x, y, z [, color] [, intensity]) - a directional light SPEC node (an ambient fill ships automatically).

metadata.name: camera
metadata.description: (x, y, z [, minDistance] [, maxDistance] [, zoomSpeed]) - a perspective camera SPEC node, looking at the origin, with optional mouse-wheel dolly clamp bounds and wheel speed. Omitted optionals get ratio defaults of the authored distance d0=|(x,y,z)| (minDistance 0.25*d0, maxDistance 4*d0, zoomSpeed 0.001); the retained scene handle attaches a wheel listener that dollies the camera along its view ray, clamped to [minDistance, maxDistance] (zoom state is ephemeral view-local, not a cel).

metadata.name: instances
metadata.description: (geometry, material, count, bufferKey) - the keystone SPEC node: N copies of one geometry as a THREE.InstancedMesh (one draw call). bufferKey is a CEL KEY STRING naming the buffer cel whose value is the SoA struct {positions: Float32Array(3N) [, colors: Float32Array(3N)]} - the spec carries the key, not the data, so it dehydrates cleanly; the scene.paint drain reads the cel and uploads per-instance transforms (residency-agnostic: any struct satisfying the shape works). instanceColor is allocated only when the struct has colors.

metadata.name: scene
metadata.description: (w, h, ...nodes) - a <canvas data-scene> VNODE carrying the scene-spec JSON (camera/light/mesh/instances nodes; optional (style ...) child). Arrives via the normal vnode pipeline; the dom replay registry dispatches it to replay.scene, which builds and RETAINS the Three object graph per canvas. 3-D twin of canvas().

metadata.name: sceneframe
metadata.description: (bufferKey, generation) - the scene.paint channel payload {key, gen}. emitsTo: a formula whose root call is sceneframe AUTO-JOINS the scene.paint channel - type =sceneframe('sheet1.B10', B11) into any cell and each generation bump re-fires it, enqueues the frame, and the drain uploads dirty instances + renders. This is how continuous sims paint WITHOUT routing per-frame state through the vnode diff (doctrine #5).

metadata.name: three.url
metadata.description: where the replayer lazy-imports three.module.js from. Default '/three.module.js' (same-origin, CSP 'self'-clean; vendored by the host - the doom asset precedent). Falls back to jsdelivr (already in origin's script-src). OPFS-cached delivery via asset.fetch would need blob: in script-src - deliberately deferred.

the 3-D paint channel. sceneframe FormulaCels declare metadata.channel:['scene.paint']; a generation/knob change buffers a {key, gen} frame here; draining uploads dirty instance transforms to the retained Three handles and renders. NOT the dom.paint vnode path - per-frame instance data never enters the vnode diff.

metadata.name: scene.paint.drain
metadata.description: Channel drain: for each buffered {key, gen} frame, for each retained scene handle whose instances reference that buffer cel key - read the SoA struct, dirty-diff against the last upload, setMatrixAt the changed instances (setColorAt when colors present), needsUpdate once, render. Guarded; never breaks a flush.

metadata.name: replay.scene
metadata.description: (el, state) - the 3-D replayer (dom.replayers entry for data-scene): on first sight of a <canvas data-scene>, lazy-import Three, build renderer + scene graph from the spec, full-upload the instance buffers, render once, and RETAIN the handle in a WeakMap keyed by the element (frame-to-frame updates flow through scene.paint, not re-parsing). A changed data-scene attr rebuilds; a disconnected element is pruned and its renderer disposed (GL context cap).
